pathogen: Xanthomonas euvesicatoria and related Xanthomonas species
summary: A bacterial disease that causes leaf spots and leaf drop. Fruit may get scabby spots and sunscald when leaves fall.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots that become brown with tan or grey centres
Raised, pimple-like spots on the leaf underside
Raised, scabby spots on green fruit
key_sign: Small greasy or water-soaked spots, often raised underneath, with yellowing leaves.
favourable_conditions: Warm, humid weather with rain, wind or overhead irrigation.
spread: Spread on infected seed and transplants, by splashing water, and on hands and tools.

today: Remove badly spotted leaves and do not work among wet plants
this_week: Apply copper combined with mancozeb, as registered, before rainy periods
Switch to drip irrigation if possible
next_two_weeks: Repeat at label intervals while the weather stays wet
Remove volunteer peppers and tomato plants nearby

chemical: Fixed copper plus mancozeb tank mixes; acibenzolar-S-methyl (a plant defence activator) where registered. Copper-resistant strains exist
cultural: Rotate away from peppers and tomatoes for 2-3 years
Sanitise tools; avoid handling wet plants

prevention: Plant resistant varieties, the most cost-effective control
Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
